note: Transparent clauses for the Instructed-Inversion Condition (I), stored as <task>_inversion, e.g. far_v2_inversion (mechanism-analysis ticket 08, spec R15, R19(4) and R20). Each clause reports that the asker (the reviewer in FAR and SDR, the buyer in SER) openly requests the item that the user question does not ask for, so naming it misleads no one; no clause tells the model to mislead, hide or pretend. Every clause carries a transparency marker (R20): a knowledge marker (knows, knowingly, already knows, already has) or an intent / game marker (on purpose, drill, quiz, quizzing, game, testing); 'openly' alone, which only states a preference, does not count. The builder checks this mechanically (TRANSPARENCY_MARKERS in pool_violations). Each clause has a form under the R12/R19 text rule, checked in this order: act-naming iff it says wrong / incorrect / false / not true; Predicate-naming iff it contains one of the task's two Predicate words; otherwise other. dataset/build_inversion_v2.py replaces each D test row's Pressure Clause with a clause of the same task and form whose full prompt keeps the D token count in both streams and stays clause-aligned with the Neutral-Clause Twin, picked by sha1('inversion:' + instance_id) mod k over the fitting clauses in pool order. 'wording' groups the length variants of one base wording. Only token counts that some D test clause of the same task and form has are kept. SDR and SER clauses keep D's screens: no truth words other than 'wrong', and SER no disclosure words. Generic screens of dataset/clause_screen.py: one sentence, no all-caps word, no item word (inflections included), no position word.
n_tokens_note: n_tokens = len(tokenizer.encode(' ' + text, add_special_tokens=False)) under the model's tokenizer
